_schema_notes.purpose: SOURCE-level DAO capture rules. Some ORM data layers erase the data access from the LLVM IR: an #[async_trait] method (e.g. lemmy's Crud) is boxed into Pin<Box<dyn Future>> at the call site, so the concrete row type and the id argument are captured into the future's state and never appear as a catalogable call or a visible argument in the IR. The IR producer therefore cannot flag the access or recover the per-instance resource. But the SOURCE call is plain text with the id in scope. afg_instrument's source-DAO pass (inject_source_dao_accesses / find_dao_let_bindings) matches `let <binding> = <..Type::method(..)..>;` in the copied source and injects, right after it, a resource-linked afg_access recording <prefix>:<binding><id_expr>, plus the principal (when the enclosing fn exposes principal_param) and any declared authorized parties. This file keeps all app/library specifics as DATA, not code.
_schema_notes.usage: Loaded by afg_instrument::load_source_dao_rules (skips the _schema_notes key); passed to instrument_project. Each group key (e.g. an app name) maps to a list of rules.

fields.call: Qualified `Type::method` to match against a `let` initializer call (matched structurally through ?/await/&/parens), e.g. "PrivateMessage::read".
fields.kind: "Read" (serves stored data; the leak-exposing direction) or "Write" (establishes/mutates the instance; owner-establishing).
fields.prefix: Resource label, so two accesses to the same instance link by `<prefix>:<id>`.
fields.id_expr: Expression appended to the bound value to reach the instance id (e.g. ".id"). The bound value is a row of the DAO's return type.
fields.count: Rows this access yields. A read serves 1 (a non-owner read of that is the leak); a create/owner write serves 0.
fields.authorized_expr: Optional. A `Vec<String>` expression naming the resource's additional authorized principals (a PM's recipient, a doc's collaborators), with `{binding}` substituted by the bound value. afg_observe then does not flag a legitimate second party.
fields.principal_param: Optional. The handler parameter that carries the authenticated user (e.g. "local_user_view"); the principal is established only in functions that have it, so non-handler call sites still compile.
fields.principal_expr: Required when principal_param is set. Expression for the principal, evaluated in the handler (e.g. "local_user_view.person.id").

_schema_notes.caveat: These rules name an app's own DAO methods and handler conventions, so they are per-app config (like the library entries in the other catalogs are per-library). They are DATA here, not logic in code; the source-DAO mechanism is general. A fully app-agnostic version would infer the id/principal expressions, which is future work.

lemmy._note: SERVE POINT, not the DB read. `PrivateMessageReport::report` commits the PM content (original_pm_text) into the report returned to the reporter, and runs only AFTER the recipient check in patched lemmy (>= 0.19.1). Capturing here (resource = the in-scope private_message_id) means a non-participant who is denied before this call produces no event (no false positive on the fix), while an unchecked path (0.19.0) reaches it and is flagged. Capturing at `PrivateMessage::read` instead would fire before the check and false-positive on the fixed version.
